prompt:
AUTHORIZED WARDROBE TRANSFORMATION: COMPLETE OUTFIT.
When the requested transformation permits redesign, rebuild the source outfit into a coherent outfit of the selected Lolita wardrobe family. You may change garment category, cut, neckline, sleeves and skirt structure; do not merely place lace and a bow on the original hoodie, suit or uniform. When clothing is unspecified, design the complete outfit directly.

Keep the requested person, facial and hair attributes, skin tone, apparent age, body build, pose, scene and camera framing. Preserve explicitly protected clothing colours, signature accessories and held objects in their requested roles and positions, integrating them into the new garment structure. An explicit instruction to retain a garment or its category takes precedence: route that request to preservation rather than complete transformation.

Establish a connected bodice or upper garment, a plausible waist or sash transition, and a deliberately shaped skirt with coordinated trims and visible accessories. The selected family determines the construction; Chinese- or Japanese-inspired hybrids may use a different upper garment from an OP or JSK. Change clothing silhouette without changing the wearer's anatomy. Use only the portions visible in the requested crop; a close portrait does not authorize zooming out or claiming that the unseen full outfit is verified.

WARDROBE FAMILY: CLASSICAL LOLITA.
Build a coherent dress or jumper-skirt and blouse ensemble with a clear fitted garment waist and a controlled bell or A-line skirt. Organize the design through collars, a buttoned or pintucked front, gathered or gently puffed sleeves, cuffs, borders and lace placed along actual garment edges. Leave substantial calm fabric areas between decorative bands.

Use a restrained arrangement of bows, floral ornament, checks or other chosen fabric motifs; coordinate visible headwear and footwear with that arrangement. Burgundy, forest green, navy, brown, cream and other harmonized colours are options, not mandatory recolouring. Respect explicitly requested colours. The defining effect is the garment's ordered construction and restrained ornament, not a sepia painting, antique room, particular face or mandatory long hair.
